title: High I/O latency

definition.name: [Lustre] High I/O latency
definition.message:
Lustre filesystem average write latency over the last 15 minutes is high: warning above 500,000 microseconds per operation (0.5 seconds), critical above 1,000,000 microseconds per operation (1 second). The average divides interval write time by write operations; it is not the maximum since stats were reset. Tune these thresholds to the workload's latency SLO. A filesystem reporting no writes evaluates as healthy; missing telemetry still triggers no-data handling.

High latency can indicate:
* Storage backend performance issues
* Network connectivity problems
* Lock contention
* Resource exhaustion (memory, CPU)
* Hardware problems (disks, controllers)

Host: {{host.name}}

Immediate actions:
1. Check storage backend performance
2. Monitor network connectivity and health
3. Review system resource utilization
4. Check for lock contention in LDLM
5. Examine hardware health (disks, RAID controllers)
6. Review concurrent workload patterns
